2. The petitioner's case in brief:
That on 2-9-2019 at about 5.30 p.m. when the petitioner was pillion rider on the two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA-01-JG-0484 from their village towards Buradagunte village, at that time, rider of the two wheeler JUDGMENT came with high speed and i n a r a s h a n d n e g l i g e n t m a n n e r , n e a r A p p a s a n a h a l l i c r o s s , o n Buradagunte-Nandanavana road, Chitamani Taluk
, in order to avoid the dog on the road, lost control of the two wheeler, fell down and caused the accident.
Due to impact, petitioner along with rider fell down and sustained injuries and his vehicle was badly damaged.
The petitioner took treatment at hospital and due to accidental injuries, petitioner suffering from disability and discomforts.

It is further stated that prior to accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, doing farming and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, he is unable to continue in the job and lost he is earning capacity.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.

3. After service of summons, respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and only respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that there is a violation of section134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The accident took place on 2-9-2019, complaint was lodged on 20-11-2019, after lapse of 78 days from the date of alleged JUDGMENT accident.
No valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.

The petitioner himself was riding the vehicle and solely negligent in causing the accident, rider of the vehicle is not covered under the policy, as such the claim petition was not maintainable for one's own negligence.
The injured was not at all wearing the prescribed ISI marked helmet and hence sustained injuries to face.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
4. From the above said pleadings three Issues are framed:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the Two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA- 01-JG-0484 on 2-9-2019 at about 5.30 p.m. near Appasanahalli cross, Buradagunte-Nadanavana road, Chintamani Taluk,
Chikkaballapura district?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?

My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 :

CD, medical bills and prescriptions, x-rays, hospital report.
9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent seriously disputed the cause and manner of the accident and nexus between the accident and injuries.
Further it was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that there was a inordinate delay of 78 days in filing the complaint.
As per the petitioner, accident has been taken place on 2-9-2019, but the complaint has lodged on 20-11-2019 and complainant has not stated any valid reasons for the said delay.
The petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle and the police to get the compensation has falsely implicated the motor cycle bearing No.5908 in the present case.

Further respondent counsel argued that the rider of the two wheeler bearing No.KA-01-JG 084 was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and hence owner of the vehicle has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and hence 2nd respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further counsel for the respondent No.2 contended that the JUDGMENT petitioner himself was riding the vehicle, but however, petitioner created a false story by misrepresenting the materials facts with regard to the alleged accident after 78 days by contending that he was proceeding as a pillion rider.

It is self negligence case, petitioner himself while riding the motor cycle fallen, hence sustained injuries and in order to get the unlawful gain, has created false story of alleged accident by implicating the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further argued that petitioner has not weared ISI marked helmet and he has sustained injuries.
Further argued that since alleged accident has taken place due to his self negligence and self fall, the claim petition against the respondent is not maintainable and prays to dismiss the petition.

10. In the line of the argument, if the evidence and materials are perused, admittedly as rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, accident has been taken place on 2-9-2019,
but the complaint has been lodged on 20-11-2019.
As per Ex-P1 FIR as the complainant was busy in P.S.Shankara Reddy Alias Shankar Reddy vs Shankar A on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101687828/

Even the complainant Kalavathi wife of the petitioner has stated the same reason in her complaint Ex-P2.

As per first information, complainant Kalavathi after the accident, she was informed that on 2-9-2020 at about 5.15 she came to know from Shankar that her husband petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle as a pillion rider along with Shankar in new unregistered TVS Jupiter motor cycle was met with an accident near Appa cross and soon after the accident, he was admitted to the near by Chintamani government hospital and as per the advice of the doctor, her husband was taken to RL Jalappa hospital at Kolar and thereafter from there he was shifted to St.John's hospital, Bangalore and thereafter after the discharge from the St.John's hospital wife of the petitioner Kalavathi came to the police station and lodged the complaint.
Thus according to the petitioner soon after the accident, her husband victim was taken to the Chintamani Government hospital.
In support of her contention, petitioner has produced Ex-P9 outpatient card fo Government hospital, JUDGMENT Chintamani.

As per which,
history of the incident is referred to as RTA unseen.
Further it is stated in Ex-P9 that patient was suffering from the head injury and bleeding from the nose and was unconscious and not responding.

11. In this regard, I would like to rely upon the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in - (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be JUDGMENT scrutinized more carefully.

12. If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.
13. Now let us verify and analyze and appreciate whether there is any indication of fabrication or conconctation or engineered to implicate innocent persons or not.

14. Further as held by Hon'ble Apex court supra in cases of delay courts are required to examine evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

In this regard, counsel for the respondent No.2 taken the contention that on the date of JUDGMENT accident, petitioner himself was riding the motor cycle and he was not a pillion rider and on that day, he was not wearing helmet and himself was riding the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and due to his self negligence accident has been taken place and hence, petitioner P.S.Shankara Reddy Alias Shankar Reddy vs Shankar A on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101687828/
4 has not maintainable and respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

On the other hand,
petitioner denied the entire contention taken by the respondent and argued that all the police documents placed on record clearly shows that petitioner was a pillion rider on the date of the accident and due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle, accident has been taken place.

In this regard, on perusal of the evidence on record as per FIR and Ex-P2 first information report, it is clearly stated in the Ex-P2 that the friend of the petitioner by name Shankar himself was driving the vehicle in a high speed, rash and negligent manner.
But since Ex-P2 first information report and FIR has accepted, as it is an after thought and chances of creating story by implicating Shankar as rider cannot be ruled out.
15. Further respondent counsel argued that petitioner JUDGMENT himself was riding the motor cycle under the influence of alcohol and due to his negligence the accident has been caused.

In this regard, on perusal of the records, OPD of government hospital, there is no mention about who has accompanied the petitioner and also which vehicle has been involved in the accident and whether the petitioner was rider or pillion rider.

Even though as per the petitioner, he was referred to R.L.Jalappahospital, Kolar from Chintamani government hospital, but no single medical records were produced to show that he was referred to R.L.Jalappa hospital.

Petitioner has produced only the report of ultrasound scan report of R.L.Jalappa hospital done on 2-9- 2019 at about 10.40 p.m.
except the ultra sound report, no prescription or wound/doctor certificate or any medical prescription is produced before this court to show that he was referred from Chintamani hospital to the R.L.Jalappa hospital and also to know about the history of accident and also details as to who has admitted and accompanied him soon after the accident.

If at all Shankar was riding motor cycle,
certainly he would have accompanied petitioenr to JUDGMENT hospital and given information about accident either to doctor or to hospital and same would be mentioned in any of hospital records, but no single hospital records peaks about who admitted to injured to hospital and details of accident and involvement of vehicle.
Which creates a serious doubt about the version of petitioner and about history of alleged accident about fact that Shankar was riding motor cycle at the time of accident.

16. Apart from this, Ex-P11 is the case summary and discharge record of the St.medical hospital produced by the petitioner himself clearly shows that wherein the history of injury has been clearly mentioned as alleged history of RTA at about 5.30 p.m. on 3-9-2019.

Further it is clearly stated that patient under the influence of alcohol at a RTA when he skid and fall from bike on 3-9-2019 at 5.30p.m. near Basavapur, Chikkaballapur district, patient lost conscious immediately after the fall.
Though PW-1 in his cross examination denied the mention of above fact.
But PW-1 has not denied the fact that petitioner was admitted to the St.John's hospital after the accident and also has not JUDGMENT denied and disputed Ex-P11 discharge summary.

Even PW- 3 doctor in his affidavit evidence at para No.2 clearly stated that "patient had reportedly sustained RTA on 2- 4-2019 near Basavapura while riding two wheeler and he was admitted to St.John's hospital on 3-9-2019.
thus, it is clear from ex-P11 that petitioner himself was riding the motor cycle under the influence of alcohol".
Even as per Ex-P25 MLC of the St.John's medical hospital, it is stated that alleged history of injury is RTA and history of bike skid and fall with loss of control + at around 5.30 p.m. on 2-9- 2019.
Thus it is clear from Ex-P25 MLC that petitioner was riding the motor cycle and due to his loss of control and negligence bike was skid and fall.

Further Ex-P26 case sheets of the St.John's medical P.S.Shankara Reddy Alias Shankar Reddy vs Shankar A on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101687828/
5 hospital, where the petitioner was admitted.

17. Apart from this, though in the charge sheet, it was reported that Shankar was riding the motor cycle and he has sustained injuries to his nose, but no single document has been produced by the petitioner to show that at the time of JUDGMENT accident, respondent No.1 was riding the motor cycle and he has also sustained the injuries.

Mere filing of the charge sheet against the respondent No.1 by holding that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 was riding the motor cycle, this court cannot come to the conclusion that respondent No.1 was riding the motor cycle, in the absence of other corroborative evidence.

Ex-P11 discharge summary and Ex- P25 MLC clearly reveals that petitioner himself was riding the motor bike under the influence of the alcohol and lost control over the vehicle and has skid and fall from the bike.

Apart from this, even the petitioner has not tried to examine the respondent No.1 and produced any document to show that as on the date of accident,
respondent No.1 was driving the vehicle.

Under such facts and circumstances the contention taken by the petitioner that Shankar was riding the motor cycle and he was pillion rider and due to the rash and negligence of the respondent No.1 accident has been taken place cannot be believable and acceptable.
Though respondent No.1 appeared before this court though his counsel, but has not adduced any evidence.
Even the JUDGMENT petitioner has not tried to prove the same by examining the respondent No.1.
Even the petitioner has not examined any one of the eye witnesses to the accident to prove that on that day, petitioner was riding as pillion rider in motor cycle.
Even not examined investigating officer to prove this contention.

Thus, it is clear from the above facts and circumstances, that on that day petitioner was riding the motor cycle under the influence of alcohol and due to his rash and negligence, he has skid and fall and sustained injuries.

When petitioner himself due to his self negligence and rashness has caused the accident and suffered injuries,
petitioner is not entitle for any compensation.
Hence having no other option I answer this issue in the negative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :

In the light of the finding on issue No.1, issue No.2 does not survive for consideration.
19. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the findings given on issues No.1 and 2 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
-: ORDER :-
The petition filed by the petitioner JUDGMENT U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
